0|53e489bc8cd9dcfe95be3e422121539250aa8221|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"Btrfs: check pending chunks when shrinking fs to avoid corruption
When we shrink the usable size of a device (its total_bytes)
all the device extent items in the device tree and attempt to relocate
the chunk of any device extent that goes beyond the new usable size for
the device. We do that after setting the new usable size (total_bytes) in
the device object
column2: so that all new allocations (and reallocations) don't

column1: use areas of the device that go beyond the new (shorter) size. However we
were not considering that before setting the new size in the device
pending chunks might have been created that use device extents that go
beyond the new size
column2: and those device extents are not yet in the device

column1: tree after we search the device tree - they are still attached to the
list of new block group for some ongoing transaction handle
only added to the device tree when the transaction handle is ended (via
btrfs_create_pending_block_groups()).
So check for pending chunks with device extents that go beyond the new
size and if any exists
column2: commit the current transaction and repeat the

column1: search in the device tree.
Not doing this it would mean we would return success to user space while
still having extents that go beyond the new size
could override those locations on the device while the fs still references
them
column2: causing all sorts of corruption and unexpected events.
